stem: In which months is the Rabi crop sown?
expl: On the basis of seasons, the crops in India have been divided into three types. Kharif crops: The Kharif crop is the summer crop or monsoon crop in India. Kharif crops are usually sown with the beginning of the first rains i.e in June- July and harvested in October - November. Major Kharif crops of India include Millets (Bajra & Jowar), Cotton, Soyabean, Sugarcane, Turmeric, Paddy (Rice), Maize, Moong (Pulses), Groundnut, Red Chillies, etc. Rabi Crops: The Rabi crop is the spring harvest or winter crop in India . It is sown in October-November last and harvested in March-April every year. Major Rabi crops in India include Wheat, Barley, Mustard, Sesame, Peas, Potatoes. Zaid Crop: This crop is grown in some parts of the country from March to July. Prominent examples are Muskmelon, Watermelon, Vegetables of Cucurbitaceae family such as bitter gourd, pumpkin, ridged gourd, etc.

stem: Which one of the following pairs (Crop — Peculiarity) is not correctly matched?

options.text: State where rice is - West Bengal grown three times in a year

options.label: c
options.text: State with largest area - Uttar Pradesh under rice production

options.label: d
options.text: Isohyets that decide - 100 cm western limit of rice production

expl: Rice is primarily a Kharif Crop. However, in India, the time of rice cultivation varies based on altitude, climate (temperature, rainfall), Soil type and water availability. In the eastern (Including West Bengal) and Southern States of the Country, the average temperature throughout the year remains favorable for rice cultivation, allowing for two or even three crops annually. Therefore, in the eastern states, mainly West Bengal, Assam, Odisha and eastern region of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar the rice crops are grown. In contrast only one crop of rice is cultivated in the northern and western part of the country. The isohyet of 100 cm of rainfall determines the western limit of rice production. According to Agricultural Statistics at a Glance, 2024-25 for the year 2024-25, in India, Uttar Pradesh has the largest area under rice production (13.82%). As per the same report, Bihar contribution of rice production is 5.53%. Therefore, the statement given in option (a), (c) and (d) are correct, while the statement given in option (b) is incorrect. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Significantly, the system of Rice Intensification known as SRI - le. System de Riziculture in French, is originated in Madagascar in 1980s and based on the cropping principles of significantly reducing plant population, improving soil conditin and irrigation methods for root and plant development and improving plant establishment methods. It is worth mentioning here that under this type of cultivation reduced seed requirement and reduced methane production as well as reduced electricity consumptions are obtained. Thus we can say all three statements are true.

stem:
With reference to the cultivation of Kharif crops in India in the last five years, consider the following statements:
1. Area under rice cultivation is the highest.
2. Area under the cultivation of jowar is more than that of oilseeds.
3. Area of cotton cultivation is more than that of sugarcane.
4. Area under sugarcane cultivation has steadily decreased.
Which of the statement/s given above is/are correct?
expl: 1. The area under rice cultivation in India, in 2014-15 was 44.1 million hectares. In 2024-25 it became 51.27 million hectares which is the highest amongst all. 2. The area under jowar cultivation 4.0 million hectares and oilseed area is 30.44 million hectares in 2024-25. Hence area under oilseed cultivation is more than Jowar cultivation. 3. The area under sugarcane cultivation 5.1 million hectare (2014-15) and 5.45 million hectares (2024-25). Hence it has not a steady decrease for sugarcane. 4. The area under cotton cultivation was 12.8 million hectares (2014-15) & 11.48 million hectares (2024-25). Hence area under cotton cultivation is more than sugar cultivation.
